mainTopic: Carrying on roofs: רב versus שמואל, רב יוסף's forgotten teaching, and how building or not building shows a claim to the roofs
overview: Background: רב holds that on roofs you may carry only within four אמות, while שמואל allows carrying across a whole roof. The amud opens with the end of the משנה's phrase 'each roof is a domain in and of itself.' That seems to support שמואל, but בי רב reread it as a restriction: you may not split your four אמות between two roofs. A ברייתא of בי שמואל, 'they have only their own roof,' is explained the same way. רב יוסף, who forgot his learning after an illness, says he never heard שמואל's teaching. His student אביי reminds him that he taught it about a large roof next to a small one, in a version that depends on people living on the roofs. רב יוסף remembers, but corrects it: the rule depends on real walls fit for living. If only the large roof has such walls, the small-roof owners have given up their claim, so even the small roof is permitted to the large roof's people. The גמרא backs this up with רב נחמן's fixed ladder and אביי's upper room with a small wall (דקה). Both show that whoever prepares the roofs for use gets them. רבא then begins to explain when the small wall leads to a prohibition instead: when it faces the owner's own garden. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה's phrase seems to fit שמואל, not רב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says each roof is 'a domain in and of itself.' That fits שמואל nicely but seems to be a problem for רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...is a domain in and of itself.' This works well for שמואל, but it is difficult for רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה's phrase 'רשות לעצמו.' It then points out that this phrase seems to support שמואל and contradict רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each roof is its own full domain, it sounds like you can carry across the entire roof. That matches שמואל. רב limits carrying on a roof to four אמות, so the phrase looks like a problem for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A domain in and of itself, a separate area
Granted, this works out (for one view)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a quote. 'רשות לעצמו' is the end of the משנה's words from the previous lines, not a new statement.

phrases.english: is a domain in and of itself.
phrases.notes: End of the quote from the משנה (the view of חכמים).

phrases.english: Granted, according to Shmuel it works well,
phrases.notes: שמואל allows carrying across the whole roof.

phrases.english: but according to Rav it is difficult.
phrases.notes: רב allows carrying only within four אמות.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרַב קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier quotation of the משנה (on the previous amud) and turns it into a challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one may carry on roofs only within four אמות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling each roof a full 'domain in and of itself' implies you may carry throughout it, which contradicts רב's four-אמות limit.

steps.title: רב's students: the משנה is a stringency, not a leniency
steps.stepSummary: בי רב explain that 'its own domain' means you may not split your four אמות across two roofs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב said in the name of רב: it means that one may not carry two cubits on this roof and two cubits on that roof.
steps.whatsHappening: רב's students answer the challenge. They reread the משנה so that it fits רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'its own domain' is not giving permission to carry across the whole roof. It is a restriction: your four אמות must all be on one roof. You cannot use two on one roof and two on the next.

keyTerms.meaning: The students of רב's academy said
He may carry or move (an object)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rereading, 'two on this roof and two on that roof,' becomes the tool the גמרא uses again in steps 5 and 6 to answer the challenge from the ברייתא of בי שמואל.

phrases.english: The school of Rav said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְטַלְטֵל שְׁתֵּי אַמּוֹת בְּגַג זֶה,
phrases.english: that one may not carry two cubits on this roof,
and two cubits on that roof.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's wording (it is a restriction, not a permission).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Its own domain' means you may carry freely across the whole roof.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Its own domain' means the four-אמות allowance cannot be split across two roofs.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's report from Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reports that בי רב said four אמות, while בי שמואל taught 'they have only their own roof.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: When we were in Babylonia, we used to say that the school of רב said in the name of רב: one may carry on it only within four cubits. And the school of שמואל taught: they have only their own roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge רב again. This step sets up the source, and the next step will explain exactly why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר remembers the two schools as being in a dispute. בי רב said four אמות, and בי שמואל taught a ברייתא saying 'they have only their own roof.' Since he presents the ברייתא as the opposite of רב's view, it seems to mean carrying across the whole roof.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
When we were in Babylonia, we would say:
the school of Rav said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בּוֹ אֶלָּא בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: one may carry on it only within four cubits,
and those of the school of Shmuel taught:
they have only their own roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 2 by bringing a ברייתא from בי שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's four-אמות view, and the 'stringency' reading given in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא presented as opposing רב says 'they have only their own roof,' which seems to allow carrying across the whole roof.

steps.title: Spelling out the meaning of 'only their own roof'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that 'only their own roof' must mean they may carry throughout the entire roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'they have only their own roof' mean? Doesn't it mean they are permitted to carry throughout the whole roof?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא seems to mean. The answer it suggests goes against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'לאו...' is not a real request for information. It is a pointed claim: the natural meaning is that the whole roof is permitted. If so, the ברייתא contradicts רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: What is 'they have only their own roof'?
Is it not that they are permitted to carry throughout all of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 3 by drawing the conclusion from the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading 'only their own roof' as permission to carry across the entire roof directly contradicts רב.

steps.title: The ברייתא is no stronger than the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: we already explained the משנה as a restriction, so the ברייתא can be explained the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this any stronger than our משנה, which we explained as meaning that one may not carry two cubits on this roof and two cubits on that roof?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. It points out that the ברייתא's wording is no clearer than the משנה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's phrase is just as open to interpretation as the משנה's phrase. Since step 2 already reread the משנה as a restriction, the same reading can work for the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Which we established, or explained, as

phrases.english: And is it stronger than our Mishnah,
which we established as meaning that one may not carry
two cubits on this roof
and two cubits on that roof?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge drawn in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the בי שמואל ברייתא against רב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumes the ברייתא's wording is clearer than the משנה's. It is not, so the same restrictive reading applies.

steps.title: The ברייתא also means no splitting between two roofs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא too means you may not carry two אמות on one roof and two on another.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too here, it means: not two cubits on this roof and two cubits on that roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the restrictive reading to the ברייתא. This makes the ברייתא fit רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They have only their own roof' means your four-אמות allowance stays on your own roof and does not stretch onto the next roof. It does not mean you may carry across the whole roof. רב's view stands.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, phrases like 'its own domain' and 'only their own roof' are restrictions. You may carry only within four אמות, and those four cannot be split between two roofs.

phrases.english: So too here,
two cubits on this roof
and two cubits on that roof (are forbidden).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי, שְׁתֵּי אַמּוֹת בְּגַג זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection in step 5 by giving the ברייתא the same reading as the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא the same restrictive way as the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא permits carrying throughout the whole roof.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only forbids splitting four אמות between two roofs, so it agrees with רב.

steps.title: רב יוסף says he never heard this teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he does not know the teaching of שמואל that was just discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I never heard this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says he does not recognize the teaching about roofs that was just mentioned. This sets up the next move, where his student reminds him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had been sick and forgot much of his learning. Here he does not recognize שמואל's ruling about roofs: that one may carry across an entire roof, as in the ברייתא of בי שמואל quoted above. This opens a short story in which אביי reminds him of what he once taught, and that teaching ends with שמואל permitting carrying on both roofs.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not disagreeing with the rule. He simply does not remember it, because his illness made him forget his learning.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I have not heard this teaching.
phrases.notes: He forgot his learning because of an illness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the teaching of בי שמואל discussed in the earlier steps by saying he does not know it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף does not recognize the teaching.

steps.title: אביי says רב יוסף taught it himself, on the case of a large and small roof
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that he himself taught this, and he points to the case it was taught on: a big roof next to a small roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You yourself told it to us. You told it to us about this case: a large roof next to a small roof. Carrying is permitted on the large roof and forbidden on the small roof.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reminds his teacher that he did teach this, and first names the case it was taught on. This prepares for the actual teaching, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The large roof is permitted because part of its edge still has wall where it sticks out past the small roof. The small roof is forbidden because its whole side opens onto the other roof. אביי brings up this case because the forgotten teaching was said about it.

keyTerms.meaning: a large roof next to a small one

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
You yourself said it to us,
and it was about this that you said it to us:
a large roof that is next to a small one —
the large one is permitted, and the small one is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The small roof is fully open to the large one, so carrying there is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's claim that he never heard the teaching by showing that he taught it himself.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יוסף did teach this teaching.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's memory of what רב יוסף taught on the case of the large and small roof.

steps.title: אביי repeats שמואל's teaching about residents on the roofs
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes what רב יוסף had taught in the name of שמואל: the rule applies only when people live on both roofs, and if nobody lives there, both roofs are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you told us about it: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They only taught this when people live on this roof and people live on that roof. Then the edge of the small roof is a wall that gets walked over. But if nobody lives on either roof, both are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי repeats the exact teaching he remembers hearing from רב יוסף. According to it, people walking back and forth between the roofs cancel the small roof's edge, but if nobody lives there, carrying on both roofs is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When people live on both roofs, they step across the line between the roofs, so the imagined wall at the small roof's edge is 'trampled' and does not count. With no residents, nobody walks across it, so the walls of the houses below are viewed as rising up and closing off each roof. This matches the teaching of בי שמואל that each group may carry only on its own roof.

keyTerms.meaning: and you told us about it
they only taught this in a case where
a trampled wall, one that people walk over and so does not count

steps.whyThisMatters: This links the forgotten teaching to שמואל's view about roofs that was discussed in the previous steps.

phrases.english: And you said to us about it:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They only taught this

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ דִּיּוּרִין עַל זֶה וְדִיּוּרִין עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: where there are residents on this roof and residents on that roof,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוְיָא לַהּ הָא דְּקָטָן מְחִיצָה נִדְרֶסֶת.
phrases.english: because the edge of the small roof is considered a trampled partition.
phrases.notes: People walk across it, so it does not count as a wall.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין דִּיּוּרִין עַל זֶה וְעַל זֶה —
phrases.english: But if there are no residents on this roof or on that one —
both are permitted.
phrases.notes: The walls of the houses below are seen as rising up and closing off each roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual content of the teaching that אביי says רב יוסף taught about the case in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The content of שמואל's teaching on the roof case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה quoting שמואל, as passed on by רב יוסף.

steps.title: רב יוסף remembers but corrects the version: it depends on walls, not residents
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he taught it differently: the rule applies only when there are real walls around each roof, and with no walls at all, both roofs are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I told you: They only taught this when there is a wall around this roof and a wall around that roof. Then the large roof is permitted because of the wall pieces left on each side of the opening, and the small roof is fully open to the large one. But if there is no wall around either roof, both are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף now remembers the teaching, but he says אביי's version is wrong. In his version the key point is real walls, not people living there, and the ending is the opposite: with no walls, both roofs are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With real walls around each roof, the large roof keeps wall pieces (גיפופי) on both sides of the opening, so it counts as closed in. The small roof is open along its whole side, so it is forbidden. Without real walls, רב יוסף does not use the idea that the house walls rise up to close off the roofs, so both roofs are forbidden. This is the opposite of אביי's ending, which permitted both.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what I told you
wall pieces left on each side of an opening

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the teaching. אביי's version: it depends on residents, and with no residents both roofs are permitted. רב יוסף's version: it depends on real walls, and with no walls both roofs are forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not denying that he taught this. He agrees he taught it, and only corrects what it said. The final line of each version gives the opposite result.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא הָכִי אֲמַרִי לְכוּ:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I said to you:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְחִיצָה עַל זֶה
phrases.english: They only taught this where there is a partition around this roof
and a partition around that roof,
because the large roof is permitted through the wall pieces on either side of the opening,
and the small roof is open along its entire length.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין מְחִיצָה לֹא עַל זֶה וְלֹא עַל זֶה —
phrases.english: But if there is no partition around this roof or around that one —
both are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's version of the teaching from step 9 and gives the correct version.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the wording and the conclusion of אביי's version, not the fact that רב יוסף taught it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule depends on real walls around each roof, not on residents, and without walls both roofs are forbidden, not permitted.

steps.title: אביי objects: you spoke about residents
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף's version, insisting that רב יוסף had taught them a rule that mentioned residents (דיורין), not walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you told us about residents!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב יוסף. He reminds him that the teaching he gave them used the word 'residents', so it cannot be only about walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10 רב יוסף said the rule depends on walls. אביי remembers the word דיורין (residents) from רב יוסף's own teaching. That word seems to fit אביי's version, where the rule depends on people living on the roofs.

phrases.english: But you told us about residents!
phrases.notes: אביי quotes the key word from רב יוסף's earlier teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's rejection in Step 10 by pointing to the word he used.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim in Step 10 that the rule depends on walls
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teaching used the word 'residents', which points to people actually living there, not to walls.

steps.title: רב יוסף explains: 'residents' means walls fit for living
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that 'residents' was shorthand for walls that make a roof fit to live in. The rule applies when both roofs have such walls. Then the big roof is permitted because of the wall pieces left on either side of the gap, and the small roof is forbidden because its whole side is open.
steps.simpleTranslation: If I said 'residents' to you, this is what I told you: they only taught this when there is a wall fit for living around this roof and a wall fit for living around that roof. The big roof is permitted because of the wall remnants, and the small roof is fully breached.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי. He says 'residents' was really a way of describing walls that make each roof a livable space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A roof with proper walls is 'fit for residence', so the word דיורין is reinterpreted as מחיצה ראויה לדירה. When both roofs are walled, the big roof keeps wall pieces (גיפופי) on both sides of the opening, so it is still enclosed and permitted. The small roof's entire side opens into the big roof (נפרץ במלואו), so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A wall that makes the area fit to live in
Wall remnants or edges left on both sides of an opening
They only taught this in the case of

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not giving up his walls version. He is explaining that 'residents' was just his way of saying 'walls that make the roof livable'.

phrases.english: If I said 'residents' to you,
this is what I told you:
They taught this only where there is a wall
fit for living around this roof
and a wall fit for living around that roof,
so the big roof is permitted because of the wall remnants
phrases.notes: The pieces of wall on both sides of the gap keep the big roof enclosed.

phrases.english: and the small roof is breached along its full width.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אֲמַרִי לְכוּ דִּיּוּרִין, הָכִי אֲמַרִי לְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection by reinterpreting the word 'residents'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Residents' means people actually living on the roofs.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Residents' means walls that make the roof fit for living. The rule applies when both roofs are walled.

steps.title: When only the big roof has walls, even the small roof is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף continues: if only the big roof has walls fit for living and the small roof does not, then even the small roof is permitted to the big roof's people. The small-roof owners showed they gave up their claim by not building walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if there is a wall fit for living around the big roof and none around the small roof, even the small roof is permitted to the people of the big roof. What is the reason? Since they did not make a wall, they removed themselves from here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a second case to his explanation. Here only the big roof is walled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building no walls shows the small-roof owners are not using their roof as a living space. They are treated as stepping aside (סלוקי סליקו נפשייהו), so the big roof's people may carry on the small roof too. This is the opposite of Step 12, where both roofs were walled and the small roof was forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted to the people of the big roof
They have completely removed themselves, giving up their claim

steps.whatToRemember: In רב יוסף's version, walls decide everything. If both roofs have walls, only the big roof is permitted. If only the big roof has walls, both roofs are permitted to the big roof's people, because the small-roof owners gave up their claim.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ מְחִיצָה רְאוּיָה לְדִירָה עַל הַגָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: But if there is a wall fit for living around the big roof,
and none fit for living around the small roof,
even the small roof is permitted to the people of the big roof.
What is the reason?
Since they did not make a wall,
they have removed themselves from here.
phrases.notes: The small-roof owners are treated as giving up their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל יֵשׁ מְחִיצָה רְאוּיָה לְדִירָה עַל הַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יוסף's answer with the opposite case, where only one roof is walled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If only the big roof has walls fit for living, the small roof is also permitted to the big roof's people, because the small-roof owners gave up their claim.

steps.title: Support from רב נחמן's fixed ladder ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares this to רב נחמן's ruling. Someone who attaches a permanent ladder to his roof may carry on all the roofs, because the others, by not doing so, gave up their claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב נחמן said: if someone made a fixed ladder to his roof, he is permitted to carry on all the roofs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel ruling of רב נחמן to support the idea that whoever does not prepare his space gives it up to the one who does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fixed ladder shows a real intention to use the roof. The neighbors did not put up ladders, so they are treated as giving up their roofs to him. This matches the reasoning of Step 13, where not building walls means giving up the roof.

keyTerms.meaning: He is permitted to carry on all the roofs
This is like what was said

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general principle: preparing a space for use gives you rights to it, and failing to prepare it means giving it up.

phrases.english: This is like what Rav Nachman said:
If someone made a fixed ladder to his roof,
he is permitted to carry on all the roofs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 13's reasoning with a parallel ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that not preparing your roof means giving it up to the neighbor who did
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's ruling about a fixed ladder

steps.title: אביי: building an upper room with a small wall permits all roofs
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that someone who builds an upper room on his roof and puts a small wall (דקה) of four in front of it may carry on all the roofs.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: if someone built an upper room on top of his house and made a small four-high wall in front of it, he is permitted to carry on all the roofs.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another case with the same idea. Building on and preparing the roof gives a person use of all the roofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building the upper room and the small wall (דקה) in front of it shows he plans to use the roof area. The other owners did nothing, so they are treated as giving up their roofs to him, just like the fixed ladder in Step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: An upper room built on the roof
A small partition or low wall

steps.whatToRemember: The fixed ladder of רב נחמן and the upper room of אביי teach the same thing: whoever actively prepares the roofs for use gets them, and those who do nothing give up their claim.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If someone built an upper room on top of his house
and made a small wall of four in front of it,
phrases.notes: A small wall 'of four,' read here as four cubits high, that opens toward the other roofs.

phrases.english: he is permitted to carry on all the roofs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בָּנָה עֲלִיָּיה עַל גַּבֵּי בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel case to רב נחמן's ladder ruling, based on the same principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Building an upper room with a small four-high wall in front of it lets the builder carry on all the roofs.

steps.title: Sometimes the small wall leads to a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a limit to אביי's ruling. The small wall that usually lets a person carry on all the roofs can sometimes lead to a prohibition instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are times when the small wall leads to a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא responds to אביי's ruling in Step 15. He says the small wall does not always help. Sometimes it causes a prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that building a small wall in front of an עלייה shows the builder is claiming the roofs, so he may carry on all of them. רבא says this is not automatic. It depends on what the wall shows about the builder's intention. Here רבא only states the principle; he describes the actual case in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The thin or small wall (the wall of four from אביי's case)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing that אביי is wrong. He agrees that the small wall usually helps. He is only pointing out a specific case where the same small wall works the other way.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Sometimes the small wall leads to prohibition,
phrases.notes: The 'small wall' is the דקה of four from אביי's ruling in Step 15.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to אביי's ruling in Step 15. The small wall normally permits carrying, but sometimes it causes a prohibition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The small wall (דקה) does not always give permission. In some cases it leads to a prohibition.

steps.title: What is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The text asks what exact situation רבא has in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. It prepares the next step, which describes the case where the small wall leads to a prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's statement in Step 16 was general. This question asks for the specific situation. It does not challenge anything.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the specific case behind רבא's general statement in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation in which the small wall leads to a prohibition instead of a permission.

steps.title: The small wall faces the garden of his house
steps.stepSummary: The case is when the small wall is built facing the garden of the man's house. Through this he shows something about his intention, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the small wall was built facing the garden of his house, for he is saying (by his actions)...
steps.whatsHappening: The text describes רבא's case: the small wall faces the man's own garden, not the other roofs. The sentence then begins to give the reason ('for he is saying') and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's case, the small wall showed that the builder was claiming the roofs. Here the wall faces his own garden. The sides toward the other roofs were sealed (as some explain). So the wall shows that his interest is his garden, not the shared roofs. That is why it does not give him the roofs, and it can even lead to a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: The garden or open area by the house
For he is saying (through his actions)

steps.confusionAlert: 'דְּאָמַר' does not mean the man actually spoke. It means his actions 'say' something about his intention. The rest of the explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea here runs through this whole סוגיא: what a person builds shows what he intends. The same small wall can permit carrying or prohibit it, depending on which way it faces.

phrases.english: where it was built facing the garden of his house,
phrases.notes: The wall faces his own garden instead of the shared roofs.

phrases.english: for he is saying (through his actions)
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17 by describing the specific case behind רבא's statement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The small wall leads to a prohibition when it faces the garden of his house. This shows his focus is his own garden and not the shared roofs. The full reason continues on the next amud.
